patches.value: Fix arbitrary t>0, set J=[t/2,3t/2], and choose compact C from H003 so u(x,s)=q for every x∉C and s∈J. To prove Lebesgue measure finite on every compact, fix arbitrary compact K⊂ℝⁿ. By M016, K is bounded. If K is empty, it is contained in every closed ball. Otherwise choose x₀∈K; boundedness supplies a finite L≥0 such that ‖x−x₀‖≤L for every x∈K. Set R₀=‖x₀‖+L+1; the triangle inequality gives ‖x‖≤R₀ for every x∈K. In either case obtain F001: ∃R₀>0, ∀x∈K, ‖x‖≤R₀. This proves the witness basis for the next paragraph.

Choose R₀ using F001 and define Q=∏_{i=1}^n[-R₀,R₀]. Each coordinate has absolute value at most ‖x‖, hence K⊆Q. The coordinate Lebesgue measure is sigma-finite: the countable measurable intervals [-k,k] cover ℝ and each has finite measure by M014, so they are a countable finite-measure cover. M013 and M014 then give μ(Q)=∏_{i=1}^n μ([-R₀,R₀])=(2R₀)^n<∞. Apply M018 to the compact K in the Hausdorff Euclidean space to conclude K is closed and hence Borel measurable; monotonicity yields μ(K)≤μ(Q)<∞. As K was arbitrary, Lebesgue measure is finite on compact sets. The Borel measurable structure on ℝⁿ is the σ-algebra generated by Euclidean opens, so opens are measurable. Joint smoothness and u=q on the open spatial complement of C throughout J imply all first spatial and time derivatives, and the second and mixed derivatives entering e_t, vanish outside C. Thus e(·,t) is continuous with compact support in C. Apply M001 to conclude e(·,t) is integrable. The same smoothness/support argument shows u_t(·,s), u_{x_j}(·,s), e(·,s), and e_t(·,s) are continuous and vanish off C for each s∈J and j=1,…,n. This proves the claimed output for arbitrary t>0.
Each ℝ coordinate with Lebesgue measure is sigma-finite because the countable intervals [−k,k] cover ℝ and M014 gives finite measure for each.
